content: I've always been a bit confused about best practices for universes in propositions that existentially quantify over types. This came up with the recently added cslib#Cslib.RelationAlgebra.Representable. I (not thinking about it too hard at the time) used the universe of the base of the representation because this seemed intuitive, but it was pointed out to me that some places in Mathlib do this differently, like having docs#Language.IsRegular and then docs#Language.isRegular_iff that generalizes to be universe-polymorphic. Not everywhere in Mathlib does this however, and I assume there is occasionally some mathematical content to consider. What is the most common practice to follow here?

I think that if you can create a definition that needs less universe variables, without giving up mathematical generality, then you should go for it.
And then you can build alternative constructors / projections that add the extra universe(s), like the _iff you mention.

am i right in thinking you can't quantify over universes themselves, so without some restriction (eg to Type 0 in IsRegular since we mostly care about finite types, and to the type of the base in Chris' case bc it turns out this suffices) you would get a different proposition for each universe you choose to quantify over? (edit: i think this is more-or-less clearly true looking at the definition of Exists as a structure)

What Johan describes is also what I've done in some mathlib formalisation (for example, docs#Manifold.IsImmersionAt --- we avoid a free universe parameter in the definition, but offer a constructor with an extra universe).

I agree with the above.
If all the different definitions (with different universe variables) are mathematically equivalent, then you definitely shouldn't add the universe variable to the definition. If possible, it might be desirable to find a definition that doesn't even quantify over a type, and only use such a definition as an alternative.

If the definition is not equivalent for the different universe levels, then you often want to keep the universe variable.
(where docs#ContinuousMap.exists_extension' is the version with the extra universe)
